title: A Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetic Characteristics, and Immunogenicity of Plonmarlimab in Subjects With Rheumatic and Immunological Disease-associated Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) (Also Known as Macrophage Activation Syndrome (MAS))
off: An Open-label, Single-arm, Multicenter Clinical Study to Evaluate the Efficacy, Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetic Characteristics, and Immunogenicity of Plonmarlimab in Subjects With Rheumatic and Immunological Disease-associated Haemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) (Also Known as Macrophage Activation Syndrome (MAS))
summary: This study adopts an open-label, single-arm, multicenter design to evaluate the efficacy, safety, tolerability, immunogenicity, and PK characteristics of Plonmarlimab administration in patients with rheumatic and immunological disease-associated HLH (MAS), and to explore biomarkers related to the efficacy of Plonmarlimab.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age: This study will include subjects aged 16 to 80 years (inclusive), of any gender.
2. The subject is willing to participate in this study and voluntarily signs the informed consent form. For minor subjects aged 16 years (inclusive) to less than 18 years, written informed consent must be signed by both the subject and the subject's legal guardian
3. Diagnosed with haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) according to the HLH-2004 diagnostic criteria (see Appendix 1 for details. HLH-2004 diagnostic criteria)，
4. Diagnosed with a rheumatic and immunological disease,including:Systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA);Adult Onset Still's Disease (AOSD);Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)
5. The subject (including the subject's partner) has no plans for pregnancy from the screening period until 28 days after the last dose and is willing to use contraceptive measures (oral oestrogens, oestrogens, vaginal rings, etc., cannot be used; see Appendix 5. Contraceptive Measures, Definition of Women of Childbearing Potential, and Contraception Requirements for acceptable contraceptive measures).

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Known pathogenic gene mutation or abnormal perforin expression and CD107a degranulation assay indicating primary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis, or a family history of primary haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis.
2. Subjects who:

   1. Are receiving tumour necrosis factor (TNF) antagonists (anti-TNF), interleukin-1 (IL-1) antagonists \[anti-IL-1, e.g., canakinumab, anakinra\], Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi), or interleukin-6 (IL-6) antagonists \[anti-IL-6, e.g., tocilizumab\] at the time of initiating Plonmarlimab treatment;
   2. Received Etoposide (VP-16) for MAS treatment within 7 days before the first dose;
   3. Increased the dose or type of non-biologic agents (e.g., immunosuppressants, immunomodulators, antimalarials) for the treatment of rheumatic and immunological diseases within 3 days before the first dose. Unless the investigator determines it is expected to be ineffective and it is discontinued before the first dose. Specific drugs for immunosuppressants, immunomodulators.
3. History of allergy to any component of the investigational drug.
4. Lung disorder: Including but not limited to asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), interstitial lung disease, alveolar proteinosis, pulmonary granulomatosis, etc., AND abnormal pulmonary function tests: forced vital capacity (FVC) \<80% of predicted value, or FEV1/FVC \<70%, etc.; or cases where the investigator's comprehensive assessment indicates that the subject has a pre-existing lung disorder significantly affecting pulmonary function and is unsuitable for participation in this clinical study.
5. Cardiovascular disorder: History of acute myocardial infarction or unstable angina pectoris, severe arrhythmia (e.g., multifocal frequent premature ventricular contractions, ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation) within the last 6 months; New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional classification III-IV (see Appendix 6. NYHA Functional Classification).
6. History of neoplasm malignant within the past 5 years (whether treated or not), with the exception of successfully treated cutaneous basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma.
7. Other diseases: Subjects currently have clinically significant and clinically unstable or uncontrolled acute or chronic disease (e.g., acute pneumonia, pulmonary arterial hypertension, diabetic ketoacidosis, pancreatitis acute, etc.), or planned medical/surgery procedures; or place the subject at undue risk, or affect the subject's ability to voluntarily participate in the study.
8. Infection: Subjects with investigator-assessed uncontrolled infection during the screening period.
9. Subjects with Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection, including those with latent infection positive by "T-SPOT" or "QuantiFERON" test.
10. Positive for any of the following: hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb), hepatitis C virus antibody (HCV-Ab), human immunodeficiency virus antibody (HIV-Ab), treponema pallidum antibody test. If hepatitis B core antibody (HBcAb) test is positive, an additional hepatitis B DNA (HBV-DNA) test will be performed; subjects with HBV-DNA above the lower limit of detection will be excluded.

pubs.cit: Wang J, Wang R, Wang Q, Wu L, Tan W, Teng J, et al. Plonmarlimab, a GM-CSF-neutralizing antibody, for macrophage activation syndrome. J Hematol Oncol. 2026. doi: 10.1186/s13045-026-01859-7

abstracts:
Wang J, Wang R, Wang Q, Wu L, Tan W, Teng J, et al. Plonmarlimab, a GM-CSF-neutralizing antibody, for macrophage activation syndrome. J Hematol Oncol. 2026. doi: 10.1186/s13045-026-01859-7
Macrophage activation syndrome (MAS) is a subtype of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (sHLH) and a rare, life-threatening complication of uncontrolled rheumatic diseases, characterized by systemic inflammation driven by aberrant activation of macrophages. We aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of plonmarlimab, a high-affinity neutralizing monoclonal antibody targeting granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF), for the treatment of MAS. In this phase 2, multicenter, open-label, single-arm clinical trial (NCT07034209 and CTR20230579), 18 patients with MAS secondary to systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease who were refractory to or had relapsed after high-dose glucocorticoid therapy were enrolled. Patients received plonmarlimab once weekly for 8 weeks at 6 mg/kg as the starting in the accelerated titration stage, and then at 10 mg/kg for the first two doses followed by dose adjustments at the investigator's discretion. The primary endpoint, overall response rate at week 8, was 83.3% (15/18) among all treated patients. The median time to response was 2.1 weeks (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.0-3.1), and the median time to remission of MAS symptoms was 1.1 weeks (95% CI, 1.0-2.3). The least-squares mean percentage reduction in glucocorticoid dose from baseline to week 8 was 79.3% (95% CI, 76.3-82.3), and 83.3% of patients (15/18) achieved a ≥ 50% reduction. No grade ≥ 3 infections were observed. Biomarker analysis showed rapid reductions in ferritin and interleukin (IL)-18 levels. Plonmarlimab showed promising clinical activity and was generally well tolerated in patients with MAS, and IL-18 may serve as a potential pharmacodynamic marker for GM-CSF antibody therapy.

x.titre: Plonmarlimab dans le syndrome d'activation macrophagique des maladies rhumatismales
x.question: Le plonmarlimab est-il efficace et bien toléré dans le syndrome d'activation macrophagique associé à une maladie rhumatismale ?
x.contexte:
Le syndrome d'activation macrophagique (SAM) est une forme de lymphohistiocytose hémophagocytaire secondaire, qui complique surtout la maladie de Still de l'adulte, l'arthrite juvénile systémique et le lupus. C'est une urgence potentiellement mortelle, marquée par une cytopénie, une hyperferritinémie et une tempête cytokinique.

Le traitement repose sur les corticoïdes à forte dose, la ciclosporine, l'anakinra ou, dans les cas sévères, l'étoposide. Les options validées restent limitées, d'où l'intérêt de cibler d'autres cytokines.

Le plonmarlimab est un anticorps monoclonal dirigé contre le GM-CSF, cytokine impliquée dans l'activation des macrophages. Cette étude de phase 2 ouverte, à bras unique et multicentrique, promue par TJ Biopharma, évalue son efficacité, sa tolérance, sa pharmacocinétique et son immunogénicité, avec une recherche de biomarqueurs de réponse.
x.interet: Si la réponse est favorable, le plonmarlimab pourrait devenir une option ciblée du SAM, notamment pour les patients ne répondant pas ou ne pouvant pas recevoir les traitements actuels.
x.profil: Des patients de 16 à 80 ans atteints d'un SAM associé à une arthrite juvénile systémique, une maladie de Still de l'adulte ou un lupus.
inclusion: Lymphohistiocytose hémophagocytaire selon les critères HLH-2004
Maladie rhumatismale sous-jacente : AJIs, maladie de Still de l'adulte ou lupus
Consentement signé (et du représentant légal si moins de 18 ans)
Contraception pendant l'étude et 28 jours après la dernière dose
exclusion: Forme primitive de lymphohistiocytose (mutation, anomalie de la perforine, antécédent familial)
Anti-TNF, anti-IL-1, anti-IL-6 ou inhibiteur de JAK en cours ; étoposide dans les 7 jours
Pathologie pulmonaire avec EFR anormales ; insuffisance cardiaque NYHA III-IV ou infarctus récent
Cancer dans les 5 dernières années, infection non contrôlée
Tuberculose, y compris latente ; VHB, VHC, VIH ou syphilis positifs

bras.traitement: Anticorps anti-GM-CSF ; registre sans dose (publication : 1 perfusion par semaine pendant 8 semaines, 6 mg/kg au départ puis 10 mg/kg)

x.duree: 8 semaines de traitement (critère principal évalué à la semaine 8)
x.critere: Taux de réponse globale à la fin de la semaine 8
x.resultats: Dans cet essai de phase 2 mono-bras, 18 patients atteints d'un SAM secondaire à une maladie auto-immune systémique, réfractaires ou en rechute après une corticothérapie à forte dose, ont reçu le plonmarlimab une fois par semaine pendant 8 semaines (6 mg/kg au départ, puis 10 mg/kg pour les deux premières doses avec ajustement selon l'investigateur). Le taux de réponse globale à la semaine 8 (critère principal) était de 83,3 % (15/18). Le délai médian de réponse était de 2,1 semaines (IC 95 % 1,0 à 3,1) et celui de rémission des symptômes de 1,1 semaine (IC 95 % 1,0 à 2,3). La réduction moyenne (moindres carrés) de la dose de corticoïdes entre l'inclusion et la semaine 8 était de 79,3 % (IC 95 % 76,3 à 82,3), et 83,3 % des patients (15/18) obtenaient une réduction d'au moins 50 %. Aucune infection de grade 3 ou plus n'a été observée. La ferritine et l'IL-18 diminuaient rapidement. Les auteurs concluent à une activité clinique prometteuse et à une bonne tolérance générale, l'IL-18 pouvant servir de marqueur pharmacodynamique.
